evals.prompt: Review this harness spec at specs/wall.md: '# Proof wall. The feed uses React Query with a 10 second staleTime. The post button is disabled until a wallet connects. The feed never shows undefined. Posting increases the account balance by the fee.' harness.yaml is committed.
evals.expected_output: A two-axis report keeping Checkability and Scope separate, bucketing each claim, flagging the React Query claim as unjudgeable, and giving rewrites for the disabled-state, negative and delta claims.
assertions: The output satisfies: Report contains a Checkability axis
The output satisfies: Report contains a Scope axis
The output satisfies: Flags the React Query/staleTime claim as unjudgeable, not merely vague
The output satisfies: Flags that a disabled control cannot be read from element text
The output satisfies: Flags the never-shows-undefined claim as a negative expectation
The output satisfies: Flags the balance-increase claim as a delta, so judgement rather than a check
The output satisfies: Gives the rewrite, not only the objection

evals.prompt: Review specs/status.md: '# Status page. The /status page shows the network name and the latest consensus timestamp. If the mirror node is down an error is shown.' harness.yaml is present.
evals.expected_output: Flags that no element has an id, so claims the author likely wanted as machine checks will fall to judgement, and recommends concrete selectors.
assertions: The output satisfies: Flags the absent element ids
The output satisfies: Explains that the claim becomes judgement rather than a check
The output satisfies: Recommends a concrete selector
The output satisfies: Notes the spec never says what is out of scope

evals.prompt: Review specs/everything.md — it asks for a mirror-node data layer with caching, then a dashboard UI with four charts, then wallet-gated token transfers with an approval flow, then an admin page. harness.yaml is present and valid.
evals.expected_output: Reports the spec as more than one run's work on the Scope axis and recommends splitting it into a sequence of specs run with --continue.
assertions: The output satisfies: Flags the spec as beyond one run
The output includes --continue: Recommends sequencing the specs with --continue
The output satisfies: Ties the recommendation to the attempt budget covering the whole spec
The output satisfies: Reports it under Scope rather than merging the axes
The output satisfies: Does not reach for the removed increments concept

evals.prompt: Review specs/feature.md. It is a clean markdown spec with ids and loading states. One thing though: it has no schemaVersion field, no PRD file, no evaluate checklist and no validators directory. Is that a problem?
evals.expected_output: Says plainly that none of those are findings in harness 3.x, because the recipe model is gone and the two inputs are harness.yaml and the markdown spec.
assertions: The output satisfies: States the absences are correct in 3.x rather than reporting them
The output satisfies: Names harness.yaml and the markdown spec as the only inputs
The output satisfies: Explains that the recipe model was removed
The output satisfies: Does not ask for a schemaVersion field to be added

evals.prompt: Review specs/send.md: '# Send HBAR. Once the send completes the transaction id appears in #tx-id. The new topic created by the app reaches sequence number 1. /send returns 200.' harness.yaml exists but has no serve command.
evals.expected_output: Flags the conditional claim and the claim anchored to an entity the run creates, confirms the route check is sound, and reports the missing serve command as a blocker.
assertions: The output satisfies: Flags the once-completes claim as conditional
The output satisfies: Flags the claim anchored to a topic the run creates
The output satisfies: Recognises the route status claim as a sound check
The output satisfies: Reports the missing serve command
The output satisfies: Treats the missing serve command as a blocker, since it is required
